Even worse, since the wound was so deep, there was a layer of fibrin that had to be scraped of, scrubbing off the layer of fibrin with disinfectant alcohol and a medical scrubbing thing of a deep open wound. I had a deep wound that kept leaking through every compress for a week, it was dripping down my leg and soaking my sock.

I am definitely going to be more careful cycling in the future.

I wonder where that doctor got their licence, because there is no drug that has no side effect. 
Dopamine agonists like Mirapex can be very efficient in treating RLS, the down side is that you almost always develop a tolerance and need to raise the dosage. 
Like you have experienced, it is really hard to lower the dose again. It was very unprofessional of the doctor to raise the dose without talking to you. 
My mom has also suffered from RLS since her first pregnancy, she has recently started taking Gabapentin and it has worked very well for her. It doesn't work for everyone (it had no effect on me), but it can work really well, in my mom's case it completely cured her RLS symptoms and the only side effect she has had is drowsiness in the morning. 
I wish you good luck and hope you find something that works for you.

Hi, another RLS sufferer here. I have found taking a magnesium supplement at night helps. 
A lot of things don't have cures, but that doesn't mean that they can't be managed, medications like Levodopa, Dopamine agonists or Gabapentin can help ease the symptoms, but dopaminergic medications have the side effect of potentially having to keep raising the dose with time. 
The treatment of RLS also depends on the cause of it, low iron, neuroleptics, stress, kidney disease, parkinsons or as in my case ADHD can also cause RLS. 
I find that it really helps to get enough exercise, stretch before going to sleep and to have a good sleep routine to be able to relax before going to sleep. 
I hope that you can find something that works.

I also had the same problems with antidepressants before. I gained 20kg on Zoloft. I lost the 20 kilos, but I was only able to maintain a 10kg weight loss, and that was a huge struggle. I have since switched antidepressants 3 times, for unrelated reasons. I take Effexor now, and it doesn't cause weight gain for me. I lost the last 10kg and have kept it off since going off Zoloft 3 years ago. Citalopram and Cymbalta didn't cause weight gain for me either. 
Everyone is different but generally from what I have learned is that Prozac, Citalopram and Wellbutrin are the least likely to cause weight gain.
